title: The Salt of Ironhollow
premise: Beatrix Dravenmoor has spent nine years swallowing poison for the crown, immune to everything except the truth: the valley of Ironhollow is a cage built to keep magic out — and him in. When the old gods stir beneath the mountain and begin answering prayers again, Beatrix learns his immunity was never an accident; he was bred as a vessel, and his soul was sold to the court beneath the mountain before he could walk. To reclaim it, he must leave the valley that made him safe, ally with a disgraced priestess of the waking gods, and bargain with a king of ash who collects names. In the end Beatrix wins back his soul by giving away his name instead — becoming no one, free at last, but unremembered by everyone he saved.
about_author: Sable Montrose is the pen name of a former line cook who claims the best research for poison plots is working a hotel kitchen. They write fantasy about people whose jobs are more dangerous than their wars.

chapters.title: The Ninth Dish
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. On the morning of the queen's feast, Beatrix tastes a dish that should kill him and doesn't — because it isn't poison, it's an offering. The old gods have answered someone's prayer through the royal kitchens. Emotional beat: quiet dread as routine cracks open.

chapters.title: Ironhollow Rules
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He reports the anomaly to the Steward of Tasters, who goes pale and orders the cook flogged. Beatrix learns the valley's founding law: no god may enter, no soul may leave. Emotional beat: the first hint that his whole life is a containment protocol.

chapters.title: What the Cook Knew
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Before dying of 'natural causes,' the flogged cook presses a bone whistle into Beatrix's hand and whispers a name: Vespera. Emotional beat: guilt and the burden of being trusted by a dead man.

chapters.title: The Priestess in the Wall
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Following the whistle's hum, Beatrix finds Vespera, a disgraced priestess hiding in the valley's foundation stones, sustained by prayers smuggled in bread. She tells him his soul was sold before his birth. Emotional beat: vertigo of identity collapse.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Poison
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix, flashback-heavy. He reconstructs his childhood: orphaned, selected, dosed. Every immunity was a brick in a vessel being built for something else. Emotional beat: grief for a self that was never his own.

chapters.title: The Steward's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The Steward catches him with Vespera and offers a choice: betray her and be promoted out of danger, or be declared tainted. Beatrix chooses neither and runs. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: Crossing the Salt Line
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The two flee the valley at night; crossing the salt boundary, Beatrix feels magic touch him for the first time — and something inside him answer. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: Road of Small Prayers
chapters.summary: POV Vespera. Traveling toward the mountain, they pass villages where the old gods grant crude miracles for terrible prices. Vespera narrates her fall from the priesthood. Emotional beat: wary companionship forming.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers Wrong
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. A village god offers Beatrix his heart's desire — knowledge of who sold his soul — for one year of his memories. He refuses; Vespera accepts a smaller price and hides what she paid. Emotional beat: temptation and mistrust seeded.

chapters.title: Ashmarket
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. In a bazaar where souls are traded like coin, they learn the court beneath the mountain buys vessels wholesale — and that Beatrix's contract is held by the King of Ash himself. Emotional beat: horror at how ordinary soul-trade is.

chapters.title: A Name on the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Vespera. She deciphers the ledger entry: the seller's signature is the Steward of Tasters, acting for the crown. The kingdom didn't protect Beatrix; it invested in him. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Royal hunters reach Ashmarket; the crown wants its vessel back before the gods can claim it. A chase through the soul-bazaar ends with Vespera captured. Emotional beat: panic, first real loss.

chapters.title: Down Is the Only Door
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Alone, Beatrix bargains passage underground with a ferryman of the drowned dead, paying with the whistle-bone and the cook's last trust. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into determination.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. He enters the subterranean court: a mirrored inversion of the palace above, where nobles wear borrowed faces. He finds Vespera imprisoned and learns prisoners here are slowly forgotten by the living. Emotional beat: dread of erasure.

chapters.title: Audience with Ash
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The King of Ash reveals the full contract: Beatrix's body will host a returning god at the next eclipse unless the debt is paid. The price of his soul: a name freely given. Emotional beat: understanding the trap — a name is all he is.

chapters.title: Vespera's Price
chapters.summary: POV Vespera. Revealed: in chapter 9 she paid with her memory of Beatrix's true name — the one thing needed to void the contract from outside. Her sacrifice becomes the key she cannot use. Emotional beat: tragic irony, love unspoken.

chapters.title: The Eclipse Rises
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. As the eclipse begins, the returning god pours into him — and finds a body immune to everything, including possession. His lifelong poisoning becomes his armor. Emotional beat: every suffering retroactively meaningful.

chapters.title: The King of Ash Unmasked
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The furious King tries to seize him bodily; Beatrix shatters the court's mirrors, freeing the stolen faces, which turn on their keeper. Emotional beat: cathartic rebellion of the erased against the collector.

chapters.title: A Name Freely Given
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. To close the contract forever, Beatrix speaks his name into the King's ledger, surrendering it willingly. The court collapses; he carries Vespera up through the breaking dark. Emotional beat: chosen loss over forced fate.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Unremembered
chapters.summary: POV Vespera. They return to Ironhollow; the valley's law dissolves as the gods withdraw. But without a name, Beatrix is a stranger even to her — she knows she owes him everything and cannot say why. Emotional beat: bittersweet cost made intimate.

chapters.title: The Taster's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. The palace records no taster named Beatrix Dravenmoor; his cell stands empty, his service unrecorded. He watches the new taster eat safely and understands what freedom costs. Emotional beat: quiet mourning for a self.

chapters.title: Salt and Seed
chapters.summary: POV Beatrix. Naming himself anew — choosing 'Beatrix' rather than reclaiming it — he plants a garden on the old salt line with Vespera, who is learning his face by heart. Some things grow back differently. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect peace.
